name: SLSA (Supply-chain Levels for Software Artifacts)
description: Framework for supply chain integrity, assessing build and source security

major_changes: Introduction of Source Track - major milestone
Distinct Build Track and Source Track

changes: Clarifications to threat model and attestation model
Verifier metadata added to VSA format

build.description: Assurance about the build process and provenance

0.name: No Guarantees
0.description: No SLSA level. Default state with no security guarantees.
0.risk: Full exposure to supply chain attacks

1.name: Build Provenance
requirements: Build provenance exists and is generated
Provenance identifies the artifact and builder

2.name: Hosted Build, Signed Provenance
2.description: Build on hosted service with signed provenance
requirements: Build on hosted platform (not developer machine)
Provenance is signed by the build service
2.verification: Verify signature from known build service

3.name: Hardened Builds
3.description: Hermetic, reproducible builds with full provenance

source.description: NEW in v1.2 - Assurance about source code integrity

1.name: Source Provenance
1.description: Source revision is tracked with provenance

2.name: Verified Source
2.description: Source changes are reviewed and verified

3.name: Hardened Source
3.description: Full source integrity with strong controls

package_ecosystem_support.note: slsa_level here records the Build Track level a published artefact can reach through the ecosystem's own provenance mechanism. An ecosystem that only distributes checksums has no Build level: Build L1 requires provenance naming the builder and the build process, and Build L2 additionally requires that a hosted build platform generate and sign it.

npm.evidence: Signed provenance attestation generated by the hosted CI platform

pypi.evidence: Attestation signed by the hosted publisher workflow

go.status: Module checksum consistency only; no build provenance
go.why: The Go checksum database records module content hashes and a signed tree head. A lookup returns the module zip h1: hash and the go.mod h1: hash and nothing about the builder or build process, so it establishes no Build Track level on its own.
provides: Tamper-evident record that a module version's content has not changed
Detection of a module rewritten after publication
does_not_provide: Description of the build process or its inputs
Signed provenance tied to a hosted build platform
go.to_claim_a_build_level: Require separate SLSA provenance for the artefact, for example generated by slsa-github-generator and verified with slsa-verifier. Verify that provenance; do not infer a level from sum.golang.org.

container_images.evidence: Signed provenance attestation attached to the image digest
